content: Mantralayam is a pilgrim town in Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh, situated on the banks of Tungabhadra River, also bordering with Karnataka State.  Mantralayam is built around the Jeeva Samadhi of Saint Sri Ragavendra Swamy (17th Century).  We had an opportunity to visit the pilgrim centre during the New Year of 2022 (Jan 1st Week) along with our family members including our family friend Sri. Venkataraghavan.  My visit was a long due after my providential blessings of Sri Ragavendra to cure my illness.  It was made possible by Sr. Venkat through a meticulous travel plan that covered a few other places around Mantralayam.  He had booked train tickets, accommodation, and local transport for the trip lasting 3 to 4 days.  We had a nice dharshan of Sri Ragavendra, Panchamuka Anjaneyar, and a Shakti Peeth.  Thanks to Sri Venkat for organizing it nicely.  We wish all the very best to you and Sow. Suhasini to conduct many such tours of pilgrimage for Senior Citizens and others in a personalized and a professional way.

Travelling on a pilgrimage tour with Venky and Suha is truly a blessing. Their jovial nature, positive energy, and genuine care make every journey enjoyable and stress-free. They meticulously plan every aspect of the trip, paying attention to even the smallest details to ensure a smooth experience for everyone.

They had taken Amma and Bala Maami on two separate pilgrimage tours - one in the North, and one down South.  Kashi, Prayagraj, Ayodhya, Chitrakoot and Naimisharanyam followed by Kaladi, Guruvayoor, Malainadu Divya Desams and Nalambalam Temples.

What sets them apart is the special care they extend to seniors. They are always attentive to individual needs, ensuring comfort, safety, and convenience throughout the pilgrimage. Their patience, kindness, and dedication allow travelers to focus on the spiritual experience while feeling completely supported.

We are deeply grateful for their commitment and wholeheartedly recommend their pilgrimage tours to anyone seeking a meaningful, well-organized, and caring travel experience.

content: Hi I am just recollecting our pilgrimage to Mahakumbh last year. Such a fantastic experience with lots of fun, thrilling experience. Words of thanks will not be enough. When everything was impossible right from ticket booking, room etc etc when I contacted you without any hesitation you encouraged me to join you, despite the fact that the group was already big and any addition will be a burden for you. Nobody would have taken such a decision without hesitation. That shows your magnanimity. I wish you success in all your future programs and my blessings will always be with you. God bless you both.

I am 85 years old and live by myself in Chennai. All my nieces and nephews are abroad.

I was Venkat’s biology teacher in school, and we have stayed in touch over the years. In December 2023, I had a fall that required hip surgery. During that difficult time, Venkat was always there whenever I needed help. By God’s grace, I am now fully mobile again.

It had long been my dream to visit Ayodhya and have darshan of Shree Ram Lalla. Since I am single and none of my relatives were able to travel with me, Venkat kindly offered to accompany me. He took care of every single detail — booking the flight tickets, arranging car travel from Lucknow, and even making sure a wheelchair was available at the temple. Nothing was overlooked.

We left Chennai on a morning flight and had darshan in Ayodhya the very same night. After that, he also took me to all the other places in Ayodhya associated with Rama, Sita, and Hanuman. Throughout the trip, Venkat was patient, cheerful, and caring. At no point did he make me feel that this was a burden or a chore.

The day before we left for Ayodhya, I had a fever of 102°F. Even amidst his busy schedule, Venkat called me several times to check on how I was doing. His positivity and encouragement gave me the strength and confidence to get ready for the trip.

He also shared pictures and updates from our journey in a WhatsApp group created by my niece, so that my relatives could follow the trip and feel reassured.

For so many of us whose relatives live abroad, or who are unable to accompany us on pilgrimages, the service that Venkat and his wife are planning is truly a Godsend. I wish them the very best with the launch of ac-company.

I will always remain deeply grateful to Venkat for his kindness, care, and support.

A Wonderful Pilgrimage to Prayagraj

When the grand Mahakumbhamela celebrations were announced in Prayagraj (Allahabad), our family deeply wanted to attend and take a holy dip. Seeing the media reports showing millions of people pouring in from all corners of the country made us feel quite worried. We constantly questioned how it would be physically possible for us to manage the journey, handle the local transportation, and navigate the venue—even with the government's elaborate round-the-clock arrangements.
It was an incredible boon for us when Venkat and Suhasini stepped forward with a plan to accompany us. They meticulously handled our travel bookings, organizing a beautiful itinerary routed via Varanasi, which allowed us to visit other holy pilgrimage centers.
Thanks to this wonderful couple, we traveled without a single difficulty or hardship. Venkat and Suhasini provided proper, timely guidance and deeply personalized attention every step of the way. Their care and dedication are truly their greatest strengths, and they turned what could have been a stressful journey into a collection of happy moments, smiles, and unforgettable memories.
Overall, this was a deeply spiritual, enjoyable, and flawless pilgrimage. It was made entirely possible by the sincere efforts and caring attitude of both Mr. and Mrs. Venkat. We, Mr & Mrs Lakshminarayanan, are immensely grateful, look forward to exploring more places with them in the future, and wish them the absolute best as they reach great heights in this noble endeavor - ACCOMPANY!

content:
I have known Venkat for over 20 years now, and he has a remarkable way of appearing at some of the most meaningful moments in my life. He is truly a brother from another mother.

Last year, around the time of the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025, I had called him for an entirely different reason. During our conversation, he casually mentioned that he was planning a pilgrimage with his family and friends to Prayagraj for the Maha Kumbh and asked, “Why don’t you join us?” It was one of those spontaneous invitations that changed everything. Had Venkat not asked me, I would almost certainly have missed what turned out to be a once-in-a-lifetime, life-changing experience.

At a time when the entire world was watching the Maha Kumbh unfold, with news channels constantly highlighting the massive crowds and logistical challenges, many people were understandably hesitant about travelling there. But Venkat had planned every detail with extraordinary care. Our route took us through Bihar, Kashi (Varanasi), and Prayagraj before returning the same way. What seemed like a daunting pilgrimage on paper became an incredibly smooth and memorable journey because of the thought and preparation that went into it.

Our group consisted of nine people, including four senior citizens, yet everything was handled seamlessly. The accommodations were simple, comfortable, and welcoming. To this day, I still wonder how Venkat managed to secure such wonderful places during one of the largest human gatherings on the planet. Every detail had been thought through.

The trip became so much more than a pilgrimage. We experienced the local culture, enjoyed authentic food across Bihar, Varanasi, and Prayagraj, visited beautiful temples, met wonderful people, and created memories that will stay with us forever. Travelling alone without my family could have felt daunting, but it never did. From the very first day, I felt as though I was travelling with my own extended family.

What made the experience truly special was not just the destinations but the people. Venkat and his wife, Suhasini, introduced me to countless small joys that often get missed in the rush of travel. Their warmth, generosity, and genuine care transformed the entire journey into something deeply personal and meaningful.

I recently learned that they are launching their own travel venture, and I honestly cannot think of people more suited for it. They are not simply itinerary planners. They are storytellers, pilgrims, explorers, and hosts who pour their personal experience, love, and attention into every journey they curate. They take care of every traveller as if they were part of their own family and go out of their way to ensure that everyone is comfortable, included, and able to experience the destination fully.

My trip with them never felt like a commercial tour. It felt like travelling with friends and family who genuinely wanted everyone around them to have an unforgettable experience. If my Maha Kumbh journey is any indication, every trip they organize will carry that same warmth, authenticity, and care.

I wish Venkat and Suhasini every success in this new venture. They have a rare gift for creating journeys that stay with people long after they return home, and I have no doubt that many more travellers will soon have memories as cherished as mine.
